key.label: Key holder and finger guard · R22
key.note: Exported R22 key holder with the bought socket and switch models. Socket routes carry R20's stated, unmeasured solder-and-wire allowance.

steps.title: Snip Off the Print Pads
steps.caption: With the part cool, snip across the exposed middle of each narrow tie. Keep the cutter away from the permanent holder and clear the wire openings.

steps.title: Solder the Sockets Off the Holder
steps.caption: With the holder off the rod and upside down on the bench, solder each socket's two wires outside the holder. Keep solder on the terminal tabs, not above them.

steps.title: Slide In the Lower-Left Socket
steps.caption: Hold the socket about 2 mm below its seat and slide it in from the left edge, above the thin guard runners, wires trailing outward. Under its seat, lift it straight up so the two bosses enter the backplate.

checks.moving: socket_0 with the stated terminal solder allowance

steps.title: Slide In the Lower-Right Socket
steps.caption: Hold the socket about 2 mm below its seat and slide it in from the right edge, above the thin guard runners, wires trailing outward. Under its seat, lift it straight up so the two bosses enter the backplate.

checks.moving: socket_2 with the stated terminal solder allowance

steps.title: Push Up the Middle Socket
steps.caption: Push it straight up from below, beside the rod position. No runner passes under it.

socket_1.moving: socket_1 with the stated terminal solder allowance

steps.title: Push Up the Upper Sockets
steps.caption: Bring each socket up about 1 mm away from the rod position, so its inner solder joint passes beside the ring arm. 2 mm below the seat, move it in and press it up.

socket_3.moving: socket_3 with the stated terminal solder allowance

socket_4.moving: socket_4 with the stated terminal solder allowance

steps.title: Tape Every Socket
steps.caption: Lay one strip of polyimide tape across each socket and its wires onto the backplate, as on R16. Press the tape ends onto the backplate with a flat tool. Keep pressure off the guard runners. The tape insulates the solder from the rod and holds the socket.

steps.title: Press In the Switches
steps.caption: Back each socket from below with a finger or flat tool, then press each switch in from above until it clicks into the plate.

steps.title: Slide Onto the Rod
steps.caption: Slide the wired holder onto the rod end-first. The rod runs through the two rings behind the lower row; the guard has no ring of its own.

steps.title: Seated
steps.caption: Final position. The index finger rests on the rod between the inner runners; the runners sit under the lower sockets' outer terminals.

xiao.label: XIAO holder · R20 body + keeper
xiao.note: Board outline from the official XIAO nRF52840 drawing. Underside solder bumps are not modelled; see the clearance map.

board.label: XIAO nRF52840 Sense board (official outline, illustrative)

steps.title: Snip Off the Print Pads
steps.caption: With the part cool, snip across the exposed middle of each narrow tie. Keep the cutter away from the permanent holder and clear the wire openings.

steps.title: Lay In the Board
steps.caption: Tilt the near end of the board up about 6 degrees, slide the USB end under the two far fingers, then lower the near end onto its ledges. Side wires stay outside the walls. Underside solder must leave room: see the clearance map in geometry-checks.json.

steps.title: Slide On the Keeper
steps.caption: Check that the board sits flat on its ledges. If solder makes it rock or sit high, stop before fitting the keeper. With the board seated, slide the keeper over the near end until its tongue clicks.

checks.note: Overlap during the slide is the keeper tongue flexing past its tooth (designed); seated overlap is zero.

steps.title: Slide Onto the Rod
steps.caption: Slide the holder onto the rod end-first. USB, camera, antenna and reset stay uncovered.

steps.title: Seated
steps.caption: Board held by the side walls, cheeks and near stops, and kept down by the keeper.

battery.label: Battery holder · R22
battery.note: The cell is drawn at the manufacturer maximum envelope.

steps.title: Snip Off the Print Pads
steps.caption: With the part cool, snip across the exposed middle of each narrow tie. Keep the cutter away from the permanent holder and clear the wire openings.

steps.title: Optional Spacer
steps.caption: If the cell is loose, slide in the thinnest spacer that stops it moving (0.4, 0.6 or 0.8 mm) on the floor first.

steps.title: Insert the Cell
steps.caption: Insert the cell through the door end, non-lead end first. The leads trail out through the centre opening. Shown sitting on the 0.4 mm spacer.

steps.title: Drop In the Door
steps.caption: Push the door straight down into its two slots until the centre tooth clicks under the lip. R22 has a longer lead-in at the slot tops, so the tooth is pushed aside more gradually. If it is still too stiff, use the trial door, which has a shallower tooth.

checks.note: Overlap near the bottom is the catch tooth flexing over the lip (designed snap), not a clash.

steps.title: Slide Onto the Rod
steps.caption: Slide the holder onto the rod end-first.

steps.title: Seated
steps.caption: Cell held by the walls and teeth without pressure; door latched.

cable.label: Cable clip · 12 wires
cable.note: Clip frame: rod axis along Z, printed flat. Wire positions follow the stated 12 x 1.5 mm packing in parameters.json.

steps.title: Snip Off the Print Pads
steps.caption: With the part cool, snip across the exposed middle of each narrow tie. Keep the cutter away from the permanent holder and clear the wire openings.

steps.title: Slide the Clip Onto the Rod
steps.caption: Align the rod loop with a free rod end and slide the clip to position. Feed the wires through the slit in the second loop.

steps.title: Feed a Wire Through the Slit
steps.caption: Feed the flexible wires one at a time and move them aside to make room. This shows the last 1.5 mm wire entering with the rest already packed in the 7 mm loop.

steps.title: Seated
steps.caption: All twelve wires inside the loop. The clip guides the harness; it is not strain relief.
